best_for: Scientists, engineers and data people who write numeric code in Python, R or MATLAB and want something that reads like a script but runs close to compiled speed.
description:
Julia is a programming language built by an open-source project with more than 1,000 contributors and released under the MIT license. It is dynamically typed and uses multiple dispatch, which means a function picks its behavior from the types of all its arguments.

In the REPL, press ] to manage packages, ; to run shell commands and ? to read help. If you load a package you don't have yet, Julia offers to install it on the spot. Project environments let you rebuild the same setup on another machine. You can spread work across threads, build web interfaces with Genie.jl or Dash.jl, and turn a program into an executable with PackageCompiler. Python code can call Julia through juliacall.

points.title: Script-like, but compiled
points.text: Julia is dynamic and interactive, yet it compiles code to native machine code through LLVM. You write quick experiments and keep them fast without a rewrite in C.

points.title: Talks to your existing code
points.text: Julia can call C, Fortran, Python, R, Java, C++ and MATLAB. The project counts over 12,000 registered packages.

points.title: juliaup is the recommended route
points.text: The Julia team recommends juliaup for normal installs: it installs Julia and lets you switch versions. The manual installers here are meant for setups that cannot use it.

points.title: Pick current or LTS
points.text: The download page lists 1.13.4 as current stable and 1.10.13 as long-term support. LTS suits teams that want fewer changes between upgrades.

points.title: Editors, not a bundled IDE
points.text: Julia ships as a command-line REPL. For a full editor you add VS Code, Jupyter, Pluto.jl, Vim, Emacs or Zed. A JetBrains plugin exists but is paid.

points.title: Installers and versions here
points.text: Windows gets 32-bit and 64-bit installers that install per-user. The Windows listing keeps 46 versions; macOS lists only the current release, with Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Linux is not listed here; Julia advises against distro packages, which are often out of date.
